pot_240_9_chip_overlaps_run_at_2132x1378.defect: an unaccepted glyph OVERLAPS the digit run. _bridged_gap returns a negative number for it and the adjacency test's `0 <= gap` lower bound therefore never saw it, so a chip stack sitting on '40.9' left a single '2' that passed every other check -- a confident 120x under-read, invariant under all 27 constant ablations. The only such read in 17785 value-producing reads on the six development recordings.

bet_chip_covered_malformed_suffix_at_205.defect: a bet_text crop whose value is entirely covered by chip sprites. One sprite edge reads as a confident '1' and the suffix reads '3B', so the crop carries no legible number at all yet shipped a confident 1.0. Caught by the suffix condition: the numeral is not terminated by 'BB'.

stack_1131_90_above_calibrated_band_at_2.defect: the client renders this seat panel far larger than any geometry the template bank was fitted on (run height 45-60 px against a calibrated band of 12-32). The bank matches a sprite fragment as a confident '7' and ships it for a stack the screen renders as 1131.90 BB -- a 162x under-read, 16 samples on this recording. Nothing measured the UPPER edge of the calibrated range.

stack_191_wide_gap_at_1272x896.png.defect: none -- this is a DELIBERATE COVERAGE LOSS, frozen so the cost is visible. The read is correct on the pixels ('191 BB'), but its widest inter-digit gap is 3px inside a 12px run (0.250 of run height), which is inside the band a LOCATED decimal has been measured to occupy (min 3/13 = 0.2308). An integer asserted from inside that band is indistinguishable from a decimal whose dot was lost to binarization, so it is refused. 47 reads on the six development recordings pay this cost.

stack_197_speck_forged_decimal_at_2054x1.defect: dot forgery: a 2x2 text-coloured speck stamped at the baseline of the 4px letter gap between '1' and '9' of the control crop was accepted as a decimal separator (only the SPLIT was checked, never the hosting gap) and shipped a confident 1.97 -- a 100x under-read. The hosting gap is 0.18 of run height; no located decimal in the 13,669-read calibration table occupies a gap under 3/13 = 0.2308, so the read is refused (unexplained_ink_in_numeral). Adversarial round-2 finding; the speck is synthetic, the crop and the speck family (chip-sprite edges, card-border ringing, the frozen '218 BB' top-edge speck) are production-real.

P2's far arm now polices glyph-scale row ink at any distance (unexplained_ink_in_numeral). Round-2 adversary A, attack D.

stack_212_90_timer_badge_at_2062x1178.pn.defect: P1 (suffix_not_bb) was the largest refusal class in the corpus and was pinned by NO test: ablating it to `if False and ...` left the whole owned CV suite green while 218 of 219 suffix_not_bb refusals came back as confident values. This crop is the strongest of them -- the seat panel carries the stack ('212.90 BB') AND a circular action-timer badge reading '12', the badge's 2-digit run wins the read, and a timer carries no 'BB' because it is not an amount. With P1 disabled the reader ships a confident 12.0 at score 0.796, a 17.7x under-read of a real stack (the same crop and the same 12.0 recorded in note 12 under the old ranking key). Round-2 adversary C finding; crop and defect both production-real.
stack_212_90_timer_badge_at_2062x1178.pn.source: Screen Recording 2026-06-21 12.41.17 AM (2062x1178, development), stack_text, t=177.0

stack_124_80_name_row_above_at_2138x1402.defect: none -- this crop is the pin for the 0.6*max_h ROW-BAND SPLIT, the other acceptance-path mechanic round-2 mutation found unpinned (collapsing every glyph into one band survived all 280 tests). Its top edge carries the tail of the player's NAME row above the value; with the split disabled the name's glyphs become ink on the numeral's own row and P2 refuses. Corpus direction of that mutant over all 18,006 retained development crops: 236 value->UNKNOWN, 0 UNKNOWN->value, 0 value->different -- coverage-only, which is why the finding is not release-blocking.
